nodes.label: A NULL cover dimension pair means the size was not recorded, not that the post has no cover
nodes.norm_label: a null cover dimension pair means the size was not recorded not that the post has no cover
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - cover-dimensions-and-ratio-reconcile [ses_f1657096affeCvcc1c5iTFodvs].md:L6217] NULL means unknown, not 1200x630. It is NOT a claim that the cover is absent. The template must therefore never render width="undefined", and must fall back to the canonical 1200x630 (the only shape the upload pipeline emits) rather than dropping the box: a box that is right in ratio but absent is a guaranteed layout shift, and a missing attribute is not.

nodes.label: The cover dimension backfill lives in the single-apply migration, not in a seed
nodes.norm_label: the cover dimension backfill lives in the single-apply migration not in a seed
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - cover-dimensions-and-ratio-reconcile [ses_f1657096affeCvcc1c5iTFodvs].md:L10273] The backfill is in the migration, not a seed. It is a fact about assets rather than content, and db/README.md already says seed/ is "never part of migration replay". As a seed, anyone applying the file would see two NULL columns and could not tell they were meant to be filled.

nodes.label: Inline aspect-ratio styles were deleted from cover tags rather than corrected to 1200/630
nodes.norm_label: inline aspect-ratio styles were deleted from cover tags rather than corrected to 1200/630
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - cover-dimensions-and-ratio-reconcile [ses_f1657096affeCvcc1c5iTFodvs].md:L10283] The aspect-ratio inline styles on covers are gone rather than rewritten: CSS beats the width/height attributes, so any inline ratio sitting next to the attributes can only contradict them. The old declarations were 16:9 on the three components and 3:2 on both post pages, and the 3:2 was reserving a box 26 percent too tall for the largest element on the page.

nodes.label: The avatar intrinsic size came from the deploy media manifest, not from the rendered box
nodes.norm_label: the avatar intrinsic size came from the deploy media manifest not from the rendered box
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - cover-dimensions-and-ratio-reconcile [ses_f1657096affeCvcc1c5iTFodvs].md:L10277] scripts/deploy/media-manifest.json records site/images/creator.webp at 800x800, filled in by migrate-media-to-r2.mjs from sharp(...).metadata() of the bytes it actually uploaded, and an anonymous range-GET plus the repo's own parseImageDimensions corroborated 800x800. The test reads the manifest entry rather than hardcoding, so a re-exported avatar makes the test fail instead of silently going stale. This replaced a 96x96 that was read off the rendered box and never matched the file.

nodes.label: The img-intrinsic-size guard asserts over every tag instead of the first regex match
nodes.norm_label: the img-intrinsic-size guard asserts over every img tag instead of the first regex match
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - cover-dimensions-and-ratio-reconcile [ses_f1657096affeCvcc1c5iTFodvs].md:L10261] The old single-match regex is why BlogHero.astro's second image, the author avatar, was never reached by the test. assetOf() classifies each tag by the expression behind its src and reports an unclassifiable one instead of skipping it, and assetsIn() asserts per file which assets must still be present so a deleted image cannot read as a pass.

nodes.label: The lcp-preload guard was rewritten to the invariant under its now-false reason, not deleted
nodes.norm_label: the lcp-preload guard was rewritten to the invariant under its now-false reason not deleted
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset-seo/2026-09-28 - cover-dimensions-and-ratio-reconcile [ses_f1657096affeCvcc1c5iTFodvs].md:L10289] It forbade the post pages from reading cover_image_(width|height) at all, on the grounds that D1 stores no such columns. That reason is now false, but the invariant under it is not, so the test now forbids the preload payload from reading a dimension into imagesrcset/imagesizes, which is where a NULL would actually print undefined into a head link.

nodes.label: A dead pacman transaction leaves /var/lib/pacman/db.lck behind and the next transaction refuses to start
nodes.norm_label: a dead pacman transaction leaves var lib pacman db lck behind and the next transaction refuses to start
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-30 - menghapus-vim-di-arch-linux [ses_f0d41aa7effeB3OPE08mH0jgSS].md:L4206] The lock file was present at 0 bytes and pacman answered galat:gagal untuk memulai transaksi (tidak dapat mengunci database) / galat:tidak dapat mengunci database: Berkas telah ada, so removing /var/lib/pacman/db.lck was required before the retry could proceed.

nodes.label: There is no standalone kwrite package; kwrite is a name kate provides, so installing it reinstalls kate
nodes.norm_label: there is no standalone kwrite package kwrite is a name kate provides so installing it reinstalls kate
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-30 - menghapus-vim-di-arch-linux [ses_f0d41aa7effeB3OPE08mH0jgSS].md:L4319] pacman -Qi kate reports Menyediakan: kwrite and Konflik Dengan: kwrite, and pacman -Ss '^kwrite$' resolves only extra/kate, so pacman -S kwrite satisfied the request by pulling kate back in after it had just been removed.
